Unpunished
un-PUN-isht
adj.
From un- (not) and punished. Webster 1828: not punished; suffered to pass without punishment. In the Authorized Version it appears almost exclusively in a negative construction — shall not be unpunished — a double negative that functions as a strong affirmation.

Biblical Definition

Unpunished occurs in Scripture chiefly to be denied. Proverbs uses the double negative for emphasis, and the emphasis is the point: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered (Proverbs 11:21). Hand join in hand pictures conspiracy, mutual pledge, the confederacy of the wicked reinforcing one another — and the numbers change nothing. Twice more the same construction lands on the man who lies in a court: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape (Proverbs 19:5). Perjury is singled out because a false witness turns the very instrument of justice into the instrument of murder, as it did at Naboth’s trial and at Christ’s. The word takes a different and more tender turn in Jeremiah, where God speaks to His own people in exile: I am with thee, saith the LORD, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished (Jeremiah 30:11). Not left unpunished, and not made a full end of — correction in measure is what distinguishes a son from a stranger.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines UNPUNISHED as not punished; suffered to escape the penalty due to an offence; free from punishment.

expand to see more

UNPUNISHED, a. — Not punished; suffered to pass without the infliction of a penalty.

Free from punishment, whether by pardon, by neglect of authority, or by escape.

In Scripture, most often used in the negative form — shall not be unpunished — which is a strong affirmation that punishment will certainly follow.

Applied both to persons and to the offences themselves; as, the crime went unpunished.

From un-, not, and punished, from Latin poena, penalty.

Key Scripture

Proverbs 11:21 — "Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered."

Proverbs 19:5 — "A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape."

Jeremiah 30:11 — "For I am with thee, saith the LORD, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished."

Proverbs 12:7 — "The wicked are overthrown, and are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand."

Modern Corruption

The observable fact that much wickedness goes unpunished in this life is the oldest argument against God’s justice, and Scripture answers it not by denying the observation but by insisting the account is not yet closed.

expand to see more

Asaph states the problem more sharply than any modern sceptic: I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. For there are no bands in their death… they are not in trouble as other men (Psalm 73:3-5). He does not dispute the data. What changed his judgment was a location: until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end. The biblical answer to unpunished wickedness is eschatological, and it requires a real final judgment with real and eternal consequence. Remove that — whether by annihilationism, universalism, or a quiet embarrassment about hell — and Proverbs 11:21 becomes untrue, since hand join in hand plainly does succeed in this world, often for a lifetime.

The pastoral counterpart is Jeremiah 30:11, and it needs saying to the other kind of sufferer. God tells a scattered, defeated people that He will not leave them altogether unpunished, and He says it as a mercy in the middle of a promise of salvation. Correction in measure is the mark of sonship; Hebrews 12:8 says that if a man is without chastisement he is not a son. The believer who finds God dealing hardly with him is not being treated as the nations are treated — of them God says He will make a full end. Measured correction and full end are two different things, and the difference is the covenant.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew naqah (H5352), to be clean, to be held innocent, to go unpunished; paqad (H6485), to visit, to punish; Greek atimoretos, unavenged; ekpheugo (G1628), to escape.

expand to see more

Hebrew naqah (H5352) — to be clean, to be acquitted, to go free; the negative lo yinnaqeh is the shall not be unpunished of Proverbs.

Hebrew naqi (H5355) — innocent, clear; the adjective from the same root, as in innocent blood.

Hebrew paqad (H6485) — to visit, to punish; I will not leave thee altogether unpunished (Jeremiah 30:11).

Greek ekpheugo (G1628) — to flee out, to escape; how shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation? (Hebrews 2:3).

Hebrew mishpat (H4941) — judgment, the verdict rightly given; the standard against which impunity is measured.

Usage

"Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished (Proverbs 11:21) — conspiracy does not alter the outcome."

"A false witness shall not be unpunished (Proverbs 19:5) — perjury singled out, because it turns justice into murder."

"I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished (Jeremiah 30:11) — measured correction as the mark of sonship."
